title: Real-Time Marching Cubes Isosurface Extraction
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a real-time Marching Cubes isosurface extraction algorithm and render the merging effect of 3 moving Metaballs.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import through ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Marching Cubes Algorithm]

Implement the complete Marching Cubes algorithm yourself (do not use the built-in MarchingCubes example class from three.js):

1. Scalar field definition - 3 Metaballs:
   f(p) = Σᵢ rᵢ² / |p - cᵢ|²
   where rᵢ = 1.0 (radius parameter), and cᵢ is the center of each ball

2. 3D grid sampling:
   - Sampling space: the cube [-3, 3]³
   - Resolution controlled by a slider (default 48³, range 28-80)
   - Calculate the scalar field value at all 8 vertices of each grid cell

3. Lookup-table triangle extraction:
   - Use the standard 256-entry edge table (edgeTable) + 256×16 triangle table (triTable)
   - Determine inside/outside according to the isolation threshold
   - Use linear interpolation along edges to obtain precise vertex positions

4. Normal calculation:
   - Use the scalar field gradient (central differences) as the vertex normal

5. Metaball motion trajectories (sinusoidal curves):
   - Ball 1: x=2·sin(t), y=2·cos(t*0.7), z=sin(t*1.3)
   - Ball 2: x=-2·cos(t*0.8), y=sin(t*1.2), z=2·cos(t)
   - Ball 3: x=sin(t*0.6)*1.5, y=-cos(t*0.9)*1.5, z=sin(t*0.5)*2

[Rendering]
(1) Use THREE.BufferGeometry for the isosurface, rebuilding the vertex data every frame
(2) Three switchable materials:
    - shiny: MeshPhysicalMaterial, metalness=0.7, roughness=0.1, color=#FF6600
    - matte: MeshLambertMaterial, color=#4CAF50
    - wireframe: MeshBasicMaterial, wireframe=true, color=#00BCD4
(3) Lighting: 2 DirectionalLights + AmbientLight
(4) OrbitControls
(5) Dark gray background color #1a1a2e

[HUD and Controls]
(6) Resolution slider (id="resolution"): range 28-80, step 4, default 48
(7) Isosurface threshold slider (id="isolation"): range 20-200, step 5, default 80
(8) Material selector (id="material"): select dropdown, options: shiny/matte/wireframe
(9) 3 ball toggles (id="ball1", id="ball2", id="ball3"): checkboxes, all selected by default
(10) HUD display:
    - Current vertex count (id="vertexCount")
    - FPS (id="fps")
    - Active ball count (id="activeBallCount")

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - resolution: current resolution
  - isolation: current isosurface threshold
  - vertexCount: total number of triangle vertices in the current frame
  - activeBalls: number of active balls (1-3)
  - fps: frame rate
  - ballPositions: [{x,y,z}, {x,y,z}, {x,y,z}] current positions of the three balls

Output a single standalone HTML file.
physics_constraints: Marching Cubes: must implement full 256-entry edge table and tri table
Scalar field: f(p) = Σ r²/|p-c|² for each active metaball
Linear interpolation on edges for vertex positions
Resolution range 28-80 must work without crash
Isolation range 20-200 must produce valid geometry
vertexCount must be > 0 when any ball is active and isolation is reasonable
Ball positions must follow specified sinusoidal trajectories
No degenerate triangles (zero-area) in output mesh
